details: Found 26 Oct as F7 of the design review of setup-turns-off-for-a-project-the-plugins-it-doe (traced by reading, not run, since it would touch live files): after setup() writes settings.json, cmd_setup calls relay_rules.sync(only={"relay"}) with ROOT = the worktree, which renders /Users/amidman/relay/CLAUDE.local.md (projects.toml [relay] file) from the worktree's rules, or prints "Not synced" and exits 1 while merges wait for a paid run. Blocks relay-s-repo-records-the-plugins-relay-developme (it runs setup in a worktree). The portable design plans that relay writes no CLAUDE.local.md at all (owner, 26 Oct); this fix may fold into that. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).

details: CONFIRMED by reading: relay_rules spec lookup is os.path.join(os.path.dirname(spec["file"]), ".claude", "kit.toml"), and spec["file"]
is the main checkout's CLAUDE.local.md (register_project uses main_checkout(root)). relay sync also does not depend on the cwd, so
"from <main>" adds nothing. Wording only; nothing wrong is written. Size: 5.
evidence: bin/relay:450: print(f"\nNot synced from a worktree: run `relay sync` from {main}.")
failing_case: `relay setup <worktree> --specs openspec` writes .claude/kit.toml [specs] in the worktree and prints "Not synced from a worktree:
run `relay sync` from <main>". Run now, relay sync reads <main>/.claude/kit.toml (relay_rules.py:85, dirname of the target file),
which has no [specs] yet, so the rendered CLAUDE.local.md lacks the spec rules and nothing says why. It should say to run it after
fix_hint: "Not synced from a worktree: run `relay sync` after this branch is merged into <default branch>."
